newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: SOCCER-JUDGE GAGS PRESS IN MARADONA PATERNITY SUIT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-JUDGE GAGS PRESS IN MARADONA PATERNITY SUIT.

text.p: An Argentine judge on Friday imposed a media gag order on reporting on a seven-month-old baby girl whose mother has filed a paternity suit against soccer star Diego Maradona.

Judge Graciela Adriana Varela sent a written warning to the media citing a U.N. convention on the rights of the child and warning them against "publishing any news or data involving this minor in the case, on pain of a fine."

The 20-year-old woman identified only as Valeria filed the suit on Monday at a Buenos Aires family court. Her lawyers expect the court to order genetic tests within a few days which they say will prove Maradona is the father of the baby girl.

The 36-year-old soccer star, married with two daughters, is already upset at the arrest and imprisonment of his manager and friend Guillermo Coppola on drug-dealing charges and said this latest scandal left him with no more strength to fight.
"They have beaten me. It's hard to accept because I've been a fighter all my life, but that's it: I've taken off my gloves, I've no more strength to fight," he told local radio.

The man who led Argentina to World Cup victory in 1986, but was twice banned for drugs and has admitted his cocaine habit, lost a paternity suit four years ago when a judge ruled he was the father of a boy in Naples, where he was playing.
He refused to submit himself to genetic tests in that case, but his lawyers have not commented on the latest suit.
Dalila Pinacho, Valeria's lawyer, told reporters Valeria had "tried several times to have Maradona admit his paternity, but he has systematically refused to do so."
